hook: The Polish pope who helped bring down communism and travelled the whole world.

pages.x: Karol Wojtyła was born in 1920 in Wadowice, a small town in Poland. By the age of 20 he had lost his mother, his brother and his father. He loved football, skiing and acting.
During the Nazi occupation he worked in a stone quarry and a chemical factory, acted in an underground theatre, and studied in secret to become a priest.
Made a priest in 1946, he took students hiking, skiing and canoeing in the mountains. In 1964 he became archbishop of Kraków.
In 1978 he was elected pope, taking the name John Paul II: the first pope from outside Italy in 455 years, and the first ever from Poland.
In 1979 he visited communist Poland, and millions came to his masses in the open air. A year later the free trade union Solidarity was born. His support helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe.
In 1981 a gunman shot him in St Peter's Square, and he nearly died. Two years later he visited his attacker in prison and forgave him.
He made more than 100 journeys to 129 countries, more than all the popes before him put together. He apologised for the Church's past wrongs, and in 2000 prayed at the Western Wall in Jerusalem.

He suffered from Parkinson's disease but kept working. Critics said he did far too little about priests who abused children. He died in 2005, millions came to Rome for his funeral, and in 2014 he was made a saint.
John Paul II led the Catholic Church for 26 years, helped end communism in Eastern Europe, and reached out to other faiths.
pts: Helped bring down communism in Eastern Europe
Visited more countries than any pope before him
